messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—small cracks are showing in the walls, but no one’s pushing yet. Keep your eyes open, your words light, and your plans quiet. The regime’s still standing, but the foundation’s shifting underfoot."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm holding its breath. Trust your instincts this month, but move carefully; the ground beneath us may shift without warning."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken yet—just rumbles in the distance. Some are sharpening their knives, others are packing their bags, but the walls are still standing, for now. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake caution for collapse."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm holding its breath. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are widening, and no one knows which way they’ll split. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels charged but unpredictable—like a storm holding its breath. Let’s stay sharp, keep our circles tight, and watch for small signs, not just the headlines."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather looks stable for now—calm skies, steady winds, and the usual routines holding. But even the most reliable forecasts can miss a shift in the air, so let’s keep our eyes open for the small signs. The garden still needs tending, quietly and carefully."*"
Sender 7: "*"The weather holds for now—no storms yet, but the wind is shifting. Some are packing umbrellas, others are still planning picnics; best to keep an eye on the horizon and trust the signs, not the forecasts."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels heavier these days—like a storm holding its breath. The usual rhythms are off, but no one’s sure if it’s the calm before something or just the wind shifting. Keep your eyes open, but no sudden moves—we don’t want to be the ones who misread the silence."*"
Sender 9: "*"The weather’s unpredictable—some days feel like the old routine, but the clouds are gathering in ways we can’t ignore. Best to keep an eye on the horizon and make sure our boots are sturdy, just in case the ground shifts under us."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather’s unpredictable—some say the winds are shifting, but the clouds still hold. Best to keep your boots dry and your doors unlocked, just in case."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—less like the old tension, more like the quiet before something shifts. The regime’s grip still holds, but the cracks are showing in ways that can’t be ignored: payments on time, inspections happening, even the newspapers correcting themselves. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for strength—this could be the calm before the storm, or the last gasp before the fall. Either way, we’re closer to the edge than we’ve been in years."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels charged but uneven—some corners hum with quiet energy, others stay still. The usual rhythms are off, like a clock winding down but not yet broken. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we’re all watching the same cracks form."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather’s getting worse—not just rain, but the kind that floods the streets before anyone realizes the dams have failed. Best to check your boots and keep the door unlocked, just in case."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels different—small cracks are showing, but no one knows if they’ll widen or be patched over. Keep your eyes open, your words careful, and your plans ready, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness—this could be the quiet before something, not nothing."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels lighter—vendors are back in the old squares, and the palace seems stuck in neutral—but don’t mistake stillness for stability. The shipping companies know something we don’t, and the stats office’s silence speaks louder than any headline. Stay sharp, but keep your plans quiet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels heavier now—not with fear, but with the quiet weight of something shifting. The usual signs are there, but the timing is still unclear: the regime’s moves suggest they’re preparing for a storm, but whether they’ll ride it out or be swept away remains to be seen. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for stability."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels heavier, but the cracks are widening—patrols shift, whispers grow louder, and even the regime’s voice rings hollow. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust the signs, not the noise."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—less fear, more fire—but the walls are still listening. The regime’s grip is tightening in some places, loosening in others; we should prepare for both the storm and the calm that might follow."*"
Sender 19: "*"The weather looks calm, but the barometer is dropping—old hands say the storm is coming, not going. Best to check your supplies quietly and keep your doors unlocked, just in case."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—small cracks are showing, but the walls are still standing. Keep your eyes open, your plans ready, and your words measured; the regime’s grip is slipping, but it hasn’t let go yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm holding its breath. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, trust only what you see with your own eyes, and keep your plans quiet but ready."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—warm one day, then suddenly you feel a chill in the air. The old trees are starting to rustle again, but no one’s sure if it’s the wind or something heavier coming. Keep your coats close, just in case."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—like the first quiet before a storm. The old rules are bending, but no one knows yet if they’ll break. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather seems calm, but the old trees are whispering—some branches creak under unseen weight. Best to keep the garden tidy and the doors unlocked, just in case the wind shifts suddenly."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels different—like a storm gathering just beyond the horizon. The usual signs are shifting, but no one knows yet if the wind will break the branches or just rattle the leaves. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t the time for reckless moves."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
